rationale: Concentrated tarragon oil produced sedation in a mouse experiment. A tincture report found more early exploration, while its thesis references drug-induced sleep timing without usable numerical results. The healthy-adult combination registration gives no posted results. Fresh tarragon and clinical Parkinson daytime sleepiness remain unresolved.

The confirmed Parkinson case measurements preceding a ginger formula and a later change during other mixed therapy do not isolate ginger. A nine-component ginger-containing decoction improved mouse stride performance and supplies no ingredient-specific human result.

Human odor and flavor studies used mustard as a stimulus. The 2024 combined tea report shows one participant stayed at a smell score of zero, and does not give a group estimate. An isolated nasal mustard constituent result does not resolve dietary ground seed in Parkinson disease.

The fragrant-sumac bark combination trial stopped after nine participants and released no efficacy analysis. A separate uncontrolled same-product study addressed urination frequency and other bladder symptoms. Neither identifies a ground Rhus coriaria fruit effect, and no Parkinson urgency direction was established.

A mouse study gives capsaicin-probe effects on a separate drug's dyskinesia response. A rat study instead used the antagonist capsazepine, and an isolated capsaicin comparison measured hyperactivity. The verified ground-cayenne meal study measured metabolites and energy expenditure. Ground cayenne and Parkinson dyskinesia remain unresolved.

The sesame swishing trial reported subjective speech difficulty, with inconsistent arm counts in the table. Existing rectal sesame combination observations also leave intelligibility and the culinary preparation unresolved.

Sesame oil has been used as an odor stimulus for diagnostic identification. An intranasal study gave no smell-function result. Neither measures olfaction after consuming cold-pressed sesame oil in Parkinson disease.

A periodontal probiotic-oil trial reports increased stimulated saliva in both arms. The original abstract does not identify the vehicle and no isolated refined soybean oil or Parkinson drooling comparison was available.

A small uncontrolled Parkinson diet follow-up reported improved anxiety with unassigned oil use. Avocado oil and CBD produced inconclusive acute tranquility differences, and a fibromyalgia placebo blend does not isolate avocado oil. The refined oil direction remains unresolved.

The original celiac-case preview establishes baseline walking difficulty but does not expose the outcome table. The broader gluten-withdrawal report and the separate baked-rye cognition study do not establish an isolated rye result for Parkinson freezing.

Concord juice had a slower pegboard time in one phase, mixed bilberry–grape juice was inconclusive, and a seed extract favored simple tapping across two follow-up visits. Preparation, motor tasks and healthy or non-Parkinson populations differ. Raw grape effects on Parkinson hand dexterity remain unresolved.

Parkinson diet-index comparisons reported associations with self-rated motivation. The pooled sofrito item and the mixed-food studies provide no verified braised-leek intake or separate apathy result.
